lens: LENS 1 — HIS ITEMS (L-01..L-23 and his six questions), read as a human with one hover at a time on POST /cooking/sessions (?ep=post-cooking-sessions, 1920×1200, default options), checked against gustify @05007957

verdicts.remains: The Endings chips are fixed. The same kind of repetition is still elsewhere: all 20 ENDPOINT METADATA hovers end with one identical paragraph about the page. Every gate host's role label still repeats the role's definition ('orchestrates — calls other functions…'). The Gates legend says 'My proposal: the station draws no node for this' five times.

Chips in the Endings row have one hover each. The host heads in the Gates row (RateLimitMiddleware, get_auth_context, build_auth_context, require_household, post_start_session ×4, start_session) and the Client's describeStartCookingError head are still three hover targets each: name, glyph and role label. The name's hover gives only 'X · function'.

His two 429s now lead with sensitive 20/60s versus global 120/60s. The twins come back elsewhere: the in-flight lane read at the edge says '429 Rate limit exceeded… · 429 Rate limit exceeded…', and the bench ENDING selector lists '429 · Rate limit exceeded. Try again shortly.' twice.
The legend sits on the row name as he asked. In its LABELS list, one sample chip stands for a whole class but carries that class's count: '[429] … 10 here' when there are two 429s.

The stage band and the 'one of 4' bracket are there. 'INPUT 1 of 2' has a bare count pill '2' next to it, so two numbers sit side by side with no unit. The column head 'subscription_tier_for +2' names a function, but its moment is 'the work'.
The 'no moment' column is gone. The metadata cards sit after the table.
Overview and risk is out of the table. 'conflict · large surface' explains only 'large surface'. The six alarm chips share one identical hover.

The bench TEST column is built, but it is an option. On the page, 7 of the 8 'proves 404' chips are tests of other functions (cancel_session, set timer, step progress). C237 is said to send 'no headers' when it sends auth_headers. Its bench chain offers a body-parse 400 although the test's JSON body is written out in the test, and says 'the body it sends' is not known. The 'arranges' chips give no test name.

Gates name their host (glyph + role) and wear icons: sensitive/global now read 'rate limiter · runs in RateLimitMiddleware'. The legend lists a gate's kind name in KINDS with no icon, and its icon in LABELS under a second, different definition.

function → condition → effect is drawn. Four things still read wrong or vague. (1) Raises one call down say 'the answer it becomes is not known' although the handler's except in the same row answers them. (2) The InvalidTokenError catch claims it 'commits, at context.py:79'; that commit never runs on that path. (3) The rate-limit switch just says 'decides the 429'. (4) TokenVerifier's face says 'can end at 401' but its hover says 'decides the 401'.
Where-it-decides labels (app-wide · at login · inside a call · in the handler) are built as an option, and the bench's nine-role filter is built. His to pick.

The function→table map is built (option; my pick is the default): green reads, orange writes, commit rules, the race on its link. Table chips still say 'only when a condition there holds' and never name the condition.

Function blocks exist only on the bench (option). The block's 'WHAT IT DOES' is category words ('decides an ending · reads or writes data'). The four functions of L-14 plus load_resolution_snapshot are not in the bench's function list (25 there, 28 in the row). In BY MOMENT, 8 function hovers have no checks or gives line at all.

They now wear the glyph, but still no role and no call depth. violations_for, derive_restrictions and load_resolution_snapshot say 'called at cooking.py:150' although assert_recipe_allergen_safe calls them. Why they have no role is answered only in D-069, not on the page.

The refresh chip names its trigger, the hooks that fetch again, each GET, the reply and the tables behind it. useStartCooking still wears the role 'fetcher' next to 'mutation', though it sends a POST.

The client cell now names describeStartCookingError, where the error comes from, and 'reads 403 → …'. The Endings hovers still say 'the screen reads it at cookingSessionModel.ts:389', and the reason-site hover titles are file:line. The text shown is a translation key ('cooking.error.start_allergen'), not the words the user sees. What the screen then does is not recorded.

The hourglass icon, the glyph per kind and the lifelines (option) show what each value affects: 429s, the 400, the 409, the claim on cooking_sessions, the commit. The idempotency_key chip wears 'on the request' next to 'request'. The legend counts 'server 1' where the row head says 'server 7'.

By default the row is folded into Gates. Its question appears as an unlabelled second sentence in the Gates head hover. Switches never say they are standard (79 of 80 endpoints carry them). The metadata card's 'pieces 3' does not name the three pieces. Two different rare pieces wear the same face 'rare · 6 of 80'.
No gap analysis between the page's blocks and the lab's six parts exists on any page. docs/design/design-context/legibility/ holds only the measure script and JSON.

Every pinned-row sub-column is on its row head, and a click lights its members. On the Client head, 'screen 1' counts the hook useStartCooking (and the refresh chip), not RecipeBrowseContainer — the chip the row's legend calls 'screen'. Standard or specialist's columns sit on the Gates head without that name.

Widen, hide and fit are built. The default view still overflows (2300px table in an 1854px box), and names still break mid-word (the measure went from 12 to 13): SessionNotFoundEr|ror, InvalidTokenErro|r, RecipeBrowseCont|ainer, FirebaseTokenVerifi|er.verify.

Chip hovers are before · checks · gives. Host heads, middleware (CORSMiddleware, RateLimitMiddleware), RecipeBrowseContainer and every metadata item still describe the kind, not the item. Several hovers carry sentences about the map ('It stands on the paths that call…', 'With a path picked…'). Several give code instead of values ('str(exc)', 'pydantic error type').

The bench is built: 8 columns in his order, selector, role filter, block, parts/size/colour, reset, copy. At 1920 the element names inside the blocks are cut off ('sensiti…', 'useStartCoo…', 'Rate limit exceeded…'). The ending selector has twin entries. Four functions are missing from the function list.
Gates: answered; they wear icons, and the legend says the station draws no node for them. Functions without a role (violations_for, derive_restrictions, get_idempotency_key): the page never says why.

verdicts.item: Q: what is this — a function?
verdicts.remains: 'sensitive · rate limiter — runs in RateLimitMiddleware' under the RateLimitMiddleware head. Every gate names its host.

verdicts.item: Q: what is fetching and from where?
verdicts.remains: The refresh chip names useActiveCooking → GET /cooking/active and useRemindersDue → GET /cooking/reminders/due, each reply and its tables. The sending hook is still labelled 'fetcher'.

Client side: the hover gives the server ending that reaches each branch. verdicts.item: Q: what are we representing in standard or specialist?

The lifelines put, on each value's line, the endings its reads can decide (429 ×2, 400, 409), the claim on cooking_sessions and the commit. The rate limiter's 429 read is the one twin left.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Proof · moment 'start_session SessionNotFoundError' · chips C225 C226 C228 C231 C235 C275 C276 'proves 404' (and their bench TEST blocks)
findings.what: A reader believes 8 tests prove this endpoint's 404 'Recipe not found'. 7 of them test other service functions and never touch this endpoint's code.
findings.evidence: Hover: 'calls the code behind the endpoint directly, not the endpoint · proves the 404 from cooking.py:156: Recipe not found'. Source tests/test_cooking.py: C225/C226 call cancel_session, C228 calls update_step_progress, C231 complete, C235 update stage, C275/C276 set timer — each with pytest.raises(SessionNotFoundError). Only C221 calls start_session. The bench's own C225 block says 'It calls cancel_session directly', yet its hover still says 'OUT proves 404 here'.
findings.fix: Join a pytest.raises test to an ending only when the function it calls is on this endpoint's path (start_session here). Drop the rest from this endpoint, or draw them apart as 'raises the same error in another function'.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Proof · C237 chips (reads the body · checks · SessionNotFoundError column), hover BEFORE
findings.what: The reader is told the test sends no headers, so it cannot tell how the test gets past the login check.
findings.evidence: Hover: 'sends no headers'. Source test_cooking.py:375-385: client.post(..., json={recipe_id, planned_portions: 2}, headers=auth_headers). The bench says 'sends no header it names' — a different, closer wording.
findings.fix: When headers= is a fixture variable, say 'sends the headers of the fixture auth_headers (their names are not read)'. Never say 'no headers'.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Proof · reads the body · 'C237 proves 400' (hollow chip); bench TEST · C237 · 'WAY 4 OF 4 · 400' and 'NOT KNOWN FROM THE TEST · the body it sends'
findings.what: The face says 'proves' on a chip that only fits. The ending it sits on is a JSON parse error that this test cannot produce. The bench says the body is unknown although it is written out in the test.
findings.evidence: The face reads 'C237 proves 400'; only the hover says 'fits 4 endings; this is one of them'. The test sends json={"recipe_id": str(uuid4()), "planned_portions": 2} — valid JSON, so 'There was an error parsing the body' is impossible. The bench chain lists that as way 4 of 4. Its 'checks it passes' lines are named by endings ('✓ 429 Rate limit exceeded'), which read as statuses the test received.
findings.fix: Put 'fits' on the face of hollow chips and keep 'proves' for solid ones. Read a literal json= argument as the body, and drop the ways it rules out (body parse, missing field). Name each passed check by its condition ('under the rate limit', 'token accepted'), not by the ending it would give.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Functions (start_session, assert_recipe_allergen_safe, _get_firebase_app, _firebase_credential) · Gates · the work · guard 'existing is not None and existing.user_id != user_id → 404'
findings.what: Raises are labelled 'the answer it becomes is not known' or 'the ending it becomes is not recorded', while the handler's except that answers them is drawn in the same row. The guard's face even says → 404.
findings.evidence: start_session: 'raises SessionNotFoundError at cooking.py:129; the answer it becomes is not known'. assert_recipe_allergen_safe: '…AllergenConflictError at recipes.py:234; the answer it becomes is not known'. _get_firebase_app: '…InvalidTokenError at verifier.py:89; the answer it becomes is not known'. Source: api/cooking.py:149-166 wraps start_session in try/except SessionNotFoundError→404 / AllergenConflictError→403 / ConcurrentCookCapError→409. auth/context.py:96-99 wraps build_auth_context (which calls verify) in except InvalidTokenError→401 'invalid token'.
findings.fix: Carry each raise up the call chain to the first except of its class on this endpoint's path (the page already holds both ends). Write 'becomes 403 Recipe contains your allergen restrictions (caught at cooking.py:159)'. Keep 'not known' only when no except of that class is on the path, and then behind 'more information' (D-017).

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Endings · 403 chip hover; Gates · the work; bench FUNCTION · assert_recipe_allergen_safe; bench ENDING · 403
findings.what: His question 'why does the 403 trigger?' has no answer anywhere: no raiser, no condition, and not the fact that it runs only when the user has allergens.
findings.evidence: 403 hover BEFORE: 'when AllergenConflictError is raised' only. The Gates row has no chip for recipes.py:233 `if derived & set(user_allergens)` or for services/cooking.py:142 `if user_allergens:`. The bench block lists 'RAISES AllergenConflictError services/recipes.py:234' with no condition and no 'becomes 403 here', and 'WHAT IT DOES: decides an ending · reads or writes data'.
findings.fix: Draw the raise's own if as a gate 'check two calls down' under assert_recipe_allergen_safe → 403. On the 403 ending, BEFORE should read: 'when assert_recipe_allergen_safe finds the recipe's ingredient-derived restrictions overlap the user's allergens (checked only when the user's profile lists allergens)'.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Endings · 404 chip; Gates · except SessionNotFoundError → 404
findings.what: The 404 has two causes; the page tells a reader only one.
findings.evidence: Catch hover: 'when SessionNotFoundError is raised, at cooking.py:140' (the recipe-is-None raise). Source services/cooking.py:124-130: replaying an Idempotency-Key that belongs to another household member's session raises SessionNotFoundError('Cooking session not found'). The handler also answers that with 404 'Recipe not found'. The page marks that raise's ending 'not recorded'.
findings.fix: List both causes on the 404's BEFORE: 'the recipe is missing or not active (:140) · the key belongs to another member's session (:129)'. Say the second is answered with 'Recipe not found' too.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Gates and decisions · the dependencies · 'except InvalidTokenError → 401' hover GIVES
findings.what: The reader is told a rejected token commits something to the database.
findings.evidence: Hover: 'answers 401: invalid token · commits, at context.py:79'. Source auth/context.py:77-79: verifier.verify(token) raises InvalidTokenError before resolve_or_create_user and before the commit at :79. That commit belongs to build_auth_context's success path.
findings.fix: List a commit under a catch only when it runs inside the except body, or after the except on a path that went through it.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Functions / Gates · FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify; ending 401 'invalid token'
findings.what: The main reason a request gets 401 'invalid token' — the token fails Firebase verification — is missing. The only raisers shown are two configuration errors.
findings.evidence: FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify's hover has only 'called by build_auth_context · 3 calls below'. Source auth/verifier.py:115-118 has `except Exception as exc: raise InvalidTokenError('firebase token verification failed') from exc`, and :107 has 'firebase-admin not installed'. The page shows only _get_firebase_app 'project id not set' (:89) and _firebase_credential 'malformed JSON' (:80).
findings.fix: Read raises inside except handlers (raise … from exc) as the function's own raises, and show them on the host and on the 401 ending's BEFORE.

findings.what: One item still has three hovers (name, glyph, role label). The name's hover says only its kind, and the role label repeats the role's definition on every host.

findings.what: Item hovers carry long sentences about how the page places paths or what the map could not read. They say nothing about the code.

On each path to that ending: which one this request takes is not recorded.' · 'its words are no fixed text: built as it raises, or none given'.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Endings 409 (fail) · Gates catch ConcurrentCookCapError · Proof C237 · Client 'reached by 409 str(exc)' · bench ENDING list; Endings 422 validation
findings.what: The words the caller gets are shown as code or as a placeholder, not as the actual text.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Functions · FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify, MockTokenVerifier.verify, identity_from_firebase_claims, _stages, _hold_hours, _label, concurrent_cook_cap_for_tier, _attach_photos; bench FUNCTION blocks
findings.what: A reader cannot tell what these functions do; the hover has only who calls it and how deep.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Gates · at the edge · switch 'environment, rate_limit_enabled'; the dependencies · switch 'TokenVerifier'
findings.what: The switches do not say what each setting does to the request.
findings.evidence: Rate switch GIVES 'decides the 429'. Its own BEFORE says the defaults are rate_limit_enabled False and environment LOCAL, which means no limit and no 429 locally, but the page never says so. TokenVerifier's face says 'can end at 401', its hover 'decides the 401'.
findings.fix: Write GIVES per arm: 'off (default, local): no rate limit, no 429 · on, or in production: both limits run'. For TokenVerifier: 'REAL → FirebaseTokenVerifier · otherwise MockTokenVerifier; either can end at 401 invalid token'.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Gates and decisions head (Standard or specialist folded in); ENDPOINT METADATA · Standard or specialist card; labels 'rare · 6 of 80' on the 403 ending and on idempotency_key
findings.what: The Standard or specialist row answers its question without saying it is that row. The 'standard' half is never drawn, and the rare pieces go unnamed on their labels and in the card.

The card shows 'pieces 3 · lacks 0' with no names; a click lights three labels. Two of those labels read 'rare · 6 of 80' but are different pieces ('can answer 403' and 'reads a repeat key').

findings.where: BY MOMENT · Client head 'screen 1' vs the chip RecipeBrowseContainer
findings.what: 'screen 1' does not count the chip the legend calls the screen.
findings.evidence: useStartCooking's hover and the refresh chip's hover both end 'counted in: screen'. RecipeBrowseContainer is labelled 'screen' in the row legend and is not counted. D-069 left the rename to 'sends it' open.

findings.where: BY MOMENT · In-flight state · idempotency_key chip; row legend
findings.what: One chip carries two near-identical labels, and the legend's count does not match the row head's.

findings.fix: Use lifetime words that cannot collide ('gone with the answer' / 'kept by the server'). Count in the unit the head uses (7 values, or 1 lane of 7).

findings.where: BY MOMENT · In-flight · rate limiter lane read at the edge; bench ENDING selector; Client 'any other status 429 ×2'

findings.fix: Carry the limit's name wherever a 429 is named ('429 · sensitive 20/60s', '429 · global 120/60s'). The build check that stops on twin items should also cover lane reads and the bench option lists.
